Photonic PDK validation¶

Open photonic PDKs ship two things for the same device: a parametric geometry cell driven by design parameters (gap, length, radius, width) and a foundry-validated compact model (SAX S-parameters, a coupling-coefficient lookup table, or a measured spectrum). This notebook verifies that both are available for the FDTD validation cases and shows the geometry and the reference data for each.

Case Geometry (gdsfactory) Reference data Source
1. Straight waveguide ubcpdk.cells.straight SAX waveguides.straight UBC SiEPIC EBeam
2. Directional coupler ubcpdk.cells.coupler κ LUT + measured opics_ebeam UBC / Cornerstone / SiEPIC
3. Ring coupling area ubcpdk.cells.ring_single κ LUT UBC / Cornerstone
4. MZI spectrum ubcpdk.cells.mzi measured spectrum + MZI model UBC SiEPIC EBeam
5. Ring spectrum ubcpdk.cells.ring_single measured spectrum UBC SiEPIC EBeam
6. Bragg spectrum gf.components.dbr measured spectrum UBC SiEPIC EBeam

The compact-model geometry and the simulation geometry use the same parameters, so a gsim.fdtd S-parameter extraction can be compared directly against the model. The Meep runs compare both 3-D and 2-D effective-index FDTD for the devices that fit the same reference data.

Measured data is fetched from pinned git revisions by tests.pdk_validation._fetch (neither the UBC .mat spectra nor the SiEPIC coupler .dat files ship in the published wheels), and the Cornerstone LUTs are read directly with xarray by tests.pdk_validation._cspdk.

In [2]:
import os
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from IPython.display import Markdown, display

from tests.pdk_validation import _validation as V

# Point GSIM_MEEP_PYTHON at a Python with `pymeep` installed (e.g. a conda env).
MEEP_PYTHON = os.environ.get("GSIM_MEEP_PYTHON", "python")
# Optional directory for the run artifacts (None -> a temporary directory).
OUTPUT_ROOT = os.environ.get("GSIM_PDK_OUTPUT") or None

# Accuracy-first per-case settings: finer mesh, a denser frequency grid and a
# tighter field-energy decay stop than the harness default, so every example is
# pushed as close to its reference as a single workstation allows.
OVERRIDES = V.high_resolution_overrides()


def _db(values):
    return 20 * np.log10(np.clip(np.abs(values), 1e-9, None))


def plot_validation(outcome, title):
    """Overlay the de-embedded Meep S-parameters on the reference target."""
    figure, axis = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 3.5))
    measured = outcome.reference.transmission_db is not None
    keys = (
        outcome.reference.sim_ports
        or tuple(outcome.reference.s_params)
        or tuple(outcome.s_params)
    )
    for name in keys:
        if name not in outcome.s_params:
            continue
        values = outcome.s_params[name]
        curve = _db(values)
        if measured:  # fiber-referenced data: compare shapes, not absolute loss
            curve = curve - np.nanmax(curve)
        axis.plot(
            outcome.wavelengths,
            curve,
            "-",
            label=f"Meep {outcome.dimension.upper()} {name}",
        )
    if outcome.reference.s_params:
        for name, values in sorted(outcome.reference.s_params.items()):
            axis.plot(
                outcome.reference.wavelengths, _db(values), "--", label=f"ref {name}"
            )
    elif outcome.reference.transmission_db is not None:
        ref_wl, ref_db = outcome.reference.transmission_db
        axis.plot(
            ref_wl, V.normalize_measured_spectrum(ref_db), "k", lw=0.8, label="measured"
        )
    axis.set(title=title, xlabel="wavelength (um)", ylabel="|S| (dB)")
    axis.legend(fontsize=8)
    figure.tight_layout()
    return figure


def run_and_report(name, title, *, dimension=None):
    """Run one validation case, plot the overlay and print agreement + budget."""
    outcome = V.run_case(
        name,
        output_dir=(str(Path(OUTPUT_ROOT) / name) if OUTPUT_ROOT else None),
        python_executable=MEEP_PYTHON,
        verbose=False,
        dimension=dimension,
        **OVERRIDES.get(name, {}),
    )
    plot_validation(outcome, title)
    plt.show()
    for port, metrics in outcome.metrics.items():
        if metrics:
            print(
                f"{port}: RMS={metrics['rms_db']:.2f} dB  "
                f"max={metrics['max_abs_db']:.2f} dB  "
                f"corr={metrics['corr']:.3f}  (n={metrics['n']})"
                if metrics.get("corr") is not None
                else f"corr=n/a  (n={metrics['n']})"
            )
    row = outcome.summary()
    size = (
        f"{row['cell_x_lambda']:.1f} x {row['cell_y_lambda']:.1f} x "
        f"{row['cell_z_lambda']:.1f} lambda"
    )
    print(
        f"{name}: {row['dimension']} res={row['resolution']} "
        f"freqs={row['num_freqs']} | cell {size} | "
        f"area {row['area_lambda2']:.0f} lambda^2 | "
        f"{row['cells'] / 1e6:.2f}M cells | compute {row['wall_seconds']:.0f} s "
        f"({row['timesteps']} steps)"
    )
    return outcome

Validation methodology¶

Each case is built at a geometry matched to its reference (the same gap/length/radius as the compact model, or the measured device). The published rerun uses the 2-D effective-index plane for every case so the complete UBC + Cornerstone + generic-PDK SiEPIC set is reproducible on one workstation. The 2-D cut is pinned to the core centre and the background is the PDK cladding (not the substrate).

Setting Value Why
resolution 30-40 px/um; MZI 5 px/um Four cells across 100 nm gaps for the coupling/ring cases. The very large MZI uses a coarse tractability run that is labelled as such.
num_freqs 101 (MZI 21) Resolves the measured ring/MZI/Bragg features; the coarse MZI is explicitly marked.
stopping field-energy decay stop_when_energy_decayed with a wall-clock safety cap; each run records its actual timesteps.
subpixel off The coarse validation window and feature-resolved mesh make subpixel averaging unnecessary and slow.
de-embedding mode n_eff Moves each monitor back to the port reference plane.
provenance recorded Each sim_config.json records PDK name, overlay, stack hash, resolved layers/materials and mesh settings.

Reference data inventory¶

Both Cornerstone (cspdk) and UBC (ubcpdk) publish the same strip directional-coupler and racetrack coupling-coefficient LUTs as xarray tables. _cspdk opens the Cornerstone LUTs directly (the cspdk package itself pins a different gdsfactory release), so the data is available without importing it.

    lut = _cspdk.load_lut(model=model)
    print(f"cspdk {model}: shape={lut.shape}")
    for dim in lut.dims:
        print(
            f"    {dim:>10}: {float(lut[dim].min()):g} .. {float(lut[dim].max()):g} um"
        )

for name in ("directional_coupler_strip.nc", "coupler_racetrack_strip.nc"):
    path = Path(ubcpdk.__file__).parent / "models" / name
    with __import__("xarray").open_dataarray(path) as array:
        print(f"ubcpdk {name}: shape={array.shape}")

Case 1 — Straight waveguide¶

Geometry (ubcpdk.cells.straight) and reference model (ubcpdk.models.waveguides.straight, SAX straight with neff=2.38, ng=4.30, loss_dB_cm=3). The model returns S(o1,o2); its phase slope gives the group index and its magnitude gives the loss — the quantities the FDTD run must reproduce.

LENGTH_UM = 100.0
s21 = np.asarray(wg_models.straight(wl=WAVELENGTHS_UM, length=LENGTH_UM)[("o1", "o2")])
phase = np.unwrap(np.angle(s21))
ng = -(WAVELENGTHS_UM**2) * np.gradient(phase, WAVELENGTHS_UM) / (2 * np.pi * LENGTH_UM)
loss_db = -20 * np.log10(np.abs(s21))

figure, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 3.5))
axes[0].plot(WAVELENGTHS_UM, ng)
axes[0].set(title="Group index", xlabel="wavelength (um)", ylabel="ng")
axes[1].plot(WAVELENGTHS_UM, loss_db)
axes[1].set(title="Propagation loss", xlabel="wavelength (um)", ylabel="loss (dB)")
figure.tight_layout()

Measured reference (SiEPIC opics_ebeam). The measured coupler S-parameters live in SiEPIC/SiEPIC_EBeam_PDK (fetched via _fetch); each block holds (frequency, |S|, phase). The o1-excited responses are shown below.

    figure, axis = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 3.5))

        title="Measured SiEPIC coupler (o1 excited)",
        xlabel="wavelength (nm)",
        ylabel="|S|",
    )
    axis.legend()
except _fetch.FetchError as error:
    print("Measured coupler unavailable:", error)

Additional PDK targets — Cornerstone and generic PDK¶

The validation set now covers the two primary PDK data sources plus the measured SiEPIC coupler:

  • UBC (ubcpdk) — the six original measured/model cases.
  • Cornerstone (cspdk.si220) — directional-coupler and racetrack coupling cases against the Cornerstone LUTs, using the Cornerstone LayerStack and derived core = WG - GRA geometry.
  • SiEPIC measured coupler — geometry from the generic photonic PDK (gf.gpdk, 220 nm Si), compared with the measured SiEPIC half-ring data.

Each target activates its own PDK (and clears gdsfactory's cross-PDK cell cache) before building the matched device. Recorded runs keep the PDK name, overlay, stack hash, and resolved material table for audit.

Summary¶

Every case is now built at a geometry matched to its reference and run with feature-resolved meshes, num_freqs=101, field-energy decay stopping, monitor de-embedding to the port reference planes, and insertion-loss normalisation for the measured spectra. run_and_report returns a ValidationOutcome whose .metrics holds RMS / max dB error and correlation per port.

Reference targets: straight -> SAX model; coupler and ring coupling area -> SAX/Cornerstone coupling LUTs at the same geometry; MZI, ring and Bragg -> measured UBC spectra (normalised).

The run cells below compare the 3-D-feasible devices with paired 2-D effective-index results, using the same compact-model or measured reference for each geometry. The MZI and the large ring/coupling cases use the 2-D effective-index plane because their 3-D grids are too large for a practical full-spectrum run. UBC and Cornerstone use their authoritative LayerStacks; the SiEPIC measured coupler is built with the generic photonic PDK (220 nm Si).

In [24]:
# Run every case in one go (long; needs GSIM_MEEP_PYTHON). Results are also
# returned as a dict for programmatic post-processing.
outcomes = V.run_all(
    python_executable=MEEP_PYTHON,
    verbose=False,
    overrides=OVERRIDES,
)
for name, outcome in outcomes.items():
    if isinstance(outcome, Exception):
        print(f"{name}: FAILED ({outcome})")
    else:
        summary = {
            port: round(m["rms_db"], 2) for port, m in outcome.metrics.items() if m
        }
        print(f"{name}: RMS dB per port {summary}")

        verbose=False,
        dimension="2d",
        **OVERRIDES.get(name, {}),
    )
    two_d_outcomes[name] = outcome
    plot_validation(outcome, f"Meep 2-D effective index vs reference — {name}")
    plt.show()
    for port, metrics in outcome.metrics.items():
        if metrics:
            print(
                f"{name} {port}: RMS={metrics['rms_db']:.2f} dB  "
                f"max={metrics['max_abs_db']:.2f} dB  corr={metrics['corr']:.3f}"
                if metrics.get("corr") is not None
                else f"max={metrics['max_abs_db']:.2f} dB  corr=n/a"
            )
    print("2-D run:", outcome.summary())

display(Markdown(V.format_summary(two_d_outcomes, title="2-D effective-index runs")))

Simulation plan and recorded run status¶

The run cells below define matched-geometry comparisons against the SAX/Cornerstone compact models or measured spectra. The recorded results are the fresh authoritative-stack runs committed under data/pdk_validation/runs/; all nine cases were re-run locally.

Measured spectra are normalized to their 99th-percentile level before computing dB errors. Compact-model S-parameters are compared at absolute level. RMS and max are dB errors; bias is mean simulation-minus-reference error. Correlation is useful for spectrally varying curves but not for nearly flat straight-waveguide transmission.

Recorded validation results (fresh authoritative-stack rerun)¶

These are the actual committed results, not an earlier narrative. The publication rerun uses the 2-D effective-index plane; the MZI is a coarse tractability run (5 px/um, 21 frequencies) and should be read as such. Poor agreement is reported honestly rather than hidden.

Case res best port RMS (dB) corr
straight 30 S21 0.01 -0.21347151767975023
coupler 30 S41 4.43 0.9977595206473594
ring_coupling 40 S41 9.47 -0.9890151543430252
mzi 5 S31 13.73 None
ring 40 S21 25.66 -0.06317225375334629
bragg 30 S11 23.37 0.2312094182647101
cspdk_coupler 30 S41 7.25 0.999814546140312
cspdk_ring_coupling 40 S41 1.91 -0.9827298481267679
siepic_coupler 40 S31 1.20 -0.9904786927076473

The straight guide is physical (|S21| ≈ 1, RMS 0.006 dB). The couplers capture the wavelength trend but still have an absolute-level offset. The ring, Bragg and coarse MZI cases remain materially discrepant and are not claimed as quantitative matches. Raw spectra, configs and debug metadata are under data/pdk_validation/runs/.
